title: React.memo, useMemo, useCallback
description: Master the core memoization APIs to prevent unnecessary re-renders in React applications.

data.text: Welcome to React.memo, useMemo, useCallback. This lesson covers practical concepts and patterns you can apply immediately in your React projects.
Understanding react.memo, usememo, usecallback requires familiarity with React fundamentals. In this section, we break down the key ideas and show how they fit into real-world applications.

terms.definition: A special function that lets you hook into React features from functional components.
Any operation that interacts with the outside world, such as data fetching, subscriptions, or DOM manipulation.
An optimization technique that stores the result of expensive function calls and returns the cached result when inputs are unchanged.
The process React uses to update the UI when state or props change.
An array of values passed to hooks like useEffect that determines when the effect should re-run.

data.title: Before You Begin
data.text: This lesson assumes you have completed the React fundamentals course. Make sure you are comfortable with components, props, and basic state management before diving into react.memo, usememo, usecallback.

data.title: Key Points to Remember
items: Always include all dependencies in the dependency array to avoid stale closures.
Use cleanup functions to prevent memory leaks and unnecessary network requests.
Memoize expensive calculations to keep renders fast.
Prefer composition over inheritance when building reusable logic.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Use the eslint-plugin-react-hooks plugin to enforce the rules of hooks and catch dependency array issues during development.
Once you understand the basics, you can combine multiple hooks to build more sophisticated behaviors. Custom hooks are the primary mechanism for reusing stateful logic across components.

data.title: Custom Hook Pattern
data.content: Encapsulate reusable logic in a custom hook that can be shared across components.

data.title: Common Pitfall
data.text: Never call hooks conditionally or inside loops. Hooks must always be called at the top level of your React function to preserve state across renders.
Real-world applications often require handling loading states, errors, and race conditions. Always account for these scenarios when implementing hooks and side effects.

data.title: Lesson Summary
points: The react.memo, usememo, usecallback pattern improves code reusability and maintainability.
Hooks must always be called at the top level of your component.
Custom hooks allow you to extract and reuse stateful logic.
The dependency array controls when effects run; include all reactive values.
Memoization can improve performance but should be used judiciously.
Always handle loading and error states in async components.
data.takeaway: Mastering react.memo, usememo, usecallback is essential for building production-ready React applications. Practice these patterns until they become second nature.
